lessons.title: Tourism, national parks and conservation

objectives: Name the tourist attractions of Cameroon
Explain benefits and problems of tourism
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify the names and locations of parks and attractions (Waza, Korup, Dja, Limbe Wildlife Centre, Lobé falls, Bafut, Foumban) and the colour of the Limbe and Kribi beaches; check current security conditions before suggesting visits.

blocks.md: **Tourism** is travelling for pleasure, rest, culture or adventure. **Domestic** tourists visit places within their own country; **international** tourists come from abroad. Tourists need **attractions**, **access** (roads, airports), **accommodation** (hotels), **security** and **services** such as guides and restaurants.

blocks.caption: Examples of attractions
blocks.alt: Three columns naming coastal, mountain and wildlife attractions.

blocks.title: Attractions of Cameroon
blocks.md:
- **Natural**: Mount Cameroon and the volcanic highlands; the beaches and the black sand of Limbe and the white sands of Kribi; waterfalls such as the Lobé falls at Kribi; crater lakes.
- **Wildlife**: national parks and reserves such as **Waza** in the Far North, **Korup** in the South-West, **Dja** in the south-east, and the **Limbe Wildlife Centre**.
- **Culture**: chiefdoms and palaces (Fon of Bafut, Foumban), festivals, crafts and music.

blocks.title: Benefits and problems
blocks.md: **Benefits**: income and **foreign exchange**, jobs (guides, drivers, hotels, craft sellers), development of roads and services, and protection of cultural heritage and nature. **Problems**: pollution and litter, damage to wildlife habitats, the spread of crime, loss of local culture, and money leaving the country if hotels are foreign-owned. Insecurity and poor roads discourage visitors.

**Conservation** is the careful use and protection of wildlife and natural environments. Governments set up **national parks** and **reserves**, ban **poaching** (illegal hunting) and trade in endangered species, use **rangers**, and teach people about nature. Local people must gain from tourism (jobs, shared income) so that they support conservation. Threats to wildlife are poaching, loss of forest to farming and logging, and conflict between humans and animals.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Tourism is not only foreigners: domestic tourism matters too.
- A national park protects both animals and plants and their habitat.
- Tourism is beneficial only if it is managed: too many visitors can damage the very sites they come to see.

blocks.title: Example 1: benefits
blocks.statement: A new hotel opens near the Limbe beach. Give two ways it helps the local community.
steps: It creates jobs for cooks, guides and cleaners.
Visitors buy local food and crafts, bringing income.

blocks.title: Example 2: poaching
blocks.statement: Why is poaching a danger to wildlife and what can be done?
steps: Poachers kill animals illegally, sometimes endangered species.
Numbers fall and species may disappear.
Rangers, laws and community education help to stop it.
blocks.answer: It reduces animal numbers; rangers, laws and education help.
